title: GTA 6's In-Game Animated TV Series, Macca & Friends, Hints at the Game's Absurd Scope
text: GTA 6's In-Game Animated TV Series, Macca & Friends, Hints at the Game's Absurd Scope | Push Square Menu Search Share Guest Guest Login | Sign Up Push Square News Reviews Features Videos Games PS Plus Guides Forums Search Keywords Guest Login or Sign Up Home Choose Topics... Manage Topics News Rockstar Games PS5 GTA 6 GTA 6's In-Game Animated TV Series, Macca & Friends, Hints at the Game's Absurd Scope Who needs real TV? by Stephen Tailby 2 hours ago Share: I think this might be the one thing about GTA 6 that's really made me aware of the sheer scale of what Rockstar Games is cooking up. Exclusively revealed via DiscussingFilm , an in-game, animated TV series named Macca & Friends has been revealed with the below teaser trailer: What strikes me about this is that the show looks exactly like the sort of thing you would see on Adult Swim. It has similar vibes to other cartoons aimed at adults, like Aqua Teen Hunger Force or Rick & Morty . What I mean is, this doesn't look like your typical throwaway gag that plays on a loop in the background. It looks like a full production on its own. It's described as a "series" in the official blurb, so it seems this will have multiple episodes you can watch within GTA 6. The show "follows the adventures of Macca the Gator and his wetland friends across the state of Leonida." This won't be the only thing you can tune into, either; according to Kinda Funny , there are multiple shows that have been created, including a "novela" and another animated show called The Johnsons . They say Rockstar "hired an animation studio" to create these things, and that seemingly includes Macca & Friends . If this is the sort of scope we can expect from just watching TV in GTA 6, it gets me excited about the level of detail and scope in the rest of the game. I actually love seeing what an infinite budget can create, and touches like these, how unnecessary they may seem, really add to the immersiveness of a world in my opinion. I’m not a GTA guy by any stretch, but i can’t wait to immerse myself in the world R* has created 0 19 nomither6 1 hour ago @Nalim That would be brilliant and honestly bump the games rating up by atleast 2 points. super cool idea 1 20 Metonymy 1 hour ago @Ravix “It also gives writers and creatives a chance to express themselves.” I’m so glad you pointed this out, as it’s the part that’s left out of so many of these types of discussions. 2 21 TechaNinja 1 hour ago I swear that police officer in the car is one of the guys in super troopers lol 1 22 RoomWithaMoose 1 hour ago @Ravix My stance is more that just because there's people that will 100% Assassin's Creed Odyssey, that doesn't mean every microbe of content was worth designing nor praising. This feels like content for content's sake. It DOES contribute to world building, but not in any notable way I think will improve the experience. 0 23 TheFakulty 1 hour ago As long as we don't have to pay on game subscription service and work to live then that will be great 0 24 Ravix 1 hour ago @RoomWithaMoose did you just compare Ubisoft to rockstar though 💀 I agree, in part, and I am a staunch supporter of open worlds only existing if the studio cares enough to make them feel real and be incredibly detailed and filled with good value content. AC games, even though I like them, only really do that with the historical stuff, and some shallow environmental stuff, the actual content and game design beyond that is not good enough to warrant it being there and there is a disconnect between how detailed the world looks and how detailed it actually is. Those games are mostly just moving through a world to follow objectives. GTA and RDR is more you existing in a world and there is a cinematic story you are a part of, but the world is just fine existing without you being a part of it. KCD achieved a similar thing with it's NPC work and questing, and blending of lifesim elements. I've even been critical of Ghost of Tsushima building their world too much like the throwaway AC style, even though their game is more polished and more cinematic, it has some of those flaws that do affect the Open World. Rockstar won't do that though, they strive to make everything matter. And this is simply an elevation of that. It will matter to people, and the player can treat it like they treat real TV. Do I like this? If yes, watch it. If no, don't. I personally enjoy adult animation and satire, so I will take a moment to watch some of these, but in place of watching something on netflix, rather than on place of playing the game. And, if I'm immersed, it should basically feel about the same as doing that, which is why they strive to do it - they want people engaged in their game for longer. 0 25 Boxmonkey 1 hour ago The wife is going to be very angry when she gets home and I’m chilling on the sofa watching tv shows in game 😬 0 26 Ravix 54 mins ago @Metonymy at this point they have basically created their own world and are hiring people to work within in that world 😅 It is the same with the soundtrack, too. It isn't just a soundtrack, it is the music of this world they created and to be part of that means something and gives artists a platform. If your music, your characters, your unique artwork is a part of this massive game, it is a huge deal. Sure the televisions could be set dressing that played static or looped still image frames, or just be turned off, but then no one would take a moment to actually appreciate the level of detail, and they would be playing the game faster and not paying attention. This is why I've always liked Rockstar. They actually care about this stuff. And they are the biggest entity in gaming culture because they always cared and built and built on this basic fundamental at their core. When passion projects succeed it should be lauded. Any studio could pump out yearly titles and basic iterations of the same thing. But we love gaming because some studios don't just do that, they care about their own passions, and this is theirs. 0 27 DogPark 49 mins ago I remember discovering an apartment in GTAV that had a small TV playing To Kill a Mockingbird, the old black and white film, in its entirety (!). I mean it was the size of a postage stamp but I was still impressed. I love all the TV shows, films and radio content in GTAV so I'm glad to see they've pushed it even further. 0 28 danzoEX 41 mins ago I want new Princess Robot Bubblegum episodes 0 29 waynesworld 35 mins ago Rockstar's attention to detail and world building is next level 0 Show Comments Leave A Comment Hold on there, you need to login to post a comment...
